2.1 Erdős 3: finite nonoptimality of diagonal pullbacks
Our contribution Our team supplies the 79-point strong-L-free witness at modulus 13, the finite
separation 79 > 78, and the complete formal certificate that every source-defined diagonal pullback
of a cyclic four-progression-free subset of ℤ/13ℤ has size at most 78 and is strictly smaller than
the retained witness. The certificate also proves the sharp cyclic four-progression-free maximum
of six, linking the witness and obstruction in one contribution.
Scope There is an explicit 79-point set 𝐵 ⊆ (ℤ/13ℤ)2
containing no configuration (𝑥, 𝑦), (𝑥, 𝑦 +
𝑑), (𝑥, 𝑦+2𝑑), (𝑥+𝑑, 𝑦) with 𝑑 ≠ 0. Every cyclic four-term-progression-free 𝐴 ⊆ ℤ/13ℤ has |𝐴| ≤ 6,
and {0, 1, 2, 4, 5, 7} attains six. Hence |𝐵| = 79 > 13|𝐴|, with 79 > 78 at the sharp cyclic maximum.
Diagonal pullbacks 𝑆𝐴 = {(𝑥, 𝑦) ∶ 𝑥 − 𝑦 ∈ 𝐴} are therefore not extremal for this finite strong-L
problem. The source-faithful bridge kernel-checks |𝑆𝐴| = 13|𝐴|, the L-free transfer and the strict
comparison with 𝐵, retaining the original 𝑥 − 𝑦 ∈ 𝐴 convention.
The valid one-way transfer from a progression-free set to an L-free set remains intact. This result
neither determines the strong-L maximum nor yields an asymptotic improvement or a solution or
refutation of Erdős 3. The exact equality contradicted here is recorded in the supplied ledger; its
status as a recognized obstacle for the parent conjecture is not established.
Verification evidence The cyclic sharpness certificate and source-faithful diagonal-pullback
bridge passed Lean 4.33.1 with standard axioms. A fresh seven-module source-only replay on 3
October 2026 checks the actual pullback cardinality, its L-free transfer and the strict comparison
with the retained 79-point witness. The original witness and row-partitioned proof are preserved;
the Boolean-to-Finset and original-predicate bridges are kernel checked. The source and receipts
identify Mathlib 0df444a360eaa60ab8c11dca51a86af692955474. No native-evaluation axiom or reused
project-local compiled object enters this replay.
Prior work and novelty assessment The team’s 79-point witness, the separation 79 > 78 and
its completed formal certificate form one finite-obstruction contribution. Peluse’s L-configuration
work provides relevant external context; the bounded review located no exact primary prior for
this finite separation and does not establish world priority. Its relevance as a recognized obstacle
for the parent conjecture remains a review question. This is one provisional finite-obstruction M1
candidate; a formalization route would be an alternative assessment of the same family.

2.3 Matrix multiplication: one-leg rigidity
A seed is one fixed stored decomposition with factor lists 𝑈, 𝑉 , 𝑊. A one-leg change alters only
one of those lists. HKS139 is the label used for the supplied decomposition data.
Our contribution Our team contributes the fixed-seed one-leg obstruction: exact rank certificates
for all nine paired-factor systems across three seeds, together with standard-kernel proofs of
the injectivity and remaining-factor uniqueness statements for all three seeds. The contribution
certifies rigidity of these known decompositions under one-leg changes.
Scope Each of three stored HKS139 seeds has rational factor lists 𝑈, 𝑉 , 𝑊 of shape 23 × 9. For
each choice of two lists, the 81 × 23 matrix formed from the rowwise Kronecker products has
rank 23. Thus fixing two factor lists uniquely determines the third through the Brent equations:
changing only that list cannot reduce its support while preserving the decomposition tensor. Exact
rational elimination verifies all nine matrices across the three seeds. The solution.json is identical
to seed 0 and adds no fourth case.
Verification evidence All three stored HKS139 seeds have standard-kernel certificates for the
UV, UW and VW rational injectivity and remaining-factor uniqueness statements. Seed 0 retains
its recorded certificate; the two additional seeds passed fresh 71-module Lean 4.33.1 replays on 3
October 2026. Endpoint axioms are only propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound. The original
factors, selected minors, integer inverse tables and all 729 tensor coefficients match their source data.
The independent exact rank checks are also retained. The result does not prove a global tensor-rank
lower bound, support-139 optimality or impossibility of a simultaneous multi-leg change.
Prior work and novelty assessment The rank-23, support-139 construction is attributed
to Smirnov/HKS, and injectivity from a left inverse is standard linear algebra. The team’s
contribution is the exact obstruction for these fixed known seeds and its source-linked certificate.
The bounded review has not established an earlier identical obstruction, a new mathematical
discovery or a nontrivial prior-library delta. Its narrow relevance to the matrix hill is concrete;
meaningful novelty remains to be established.

Local record partial-a135508 | Target source
Our contribution We supply the unconditional prime-index gcd criterion, the two sufficient
congruence classes, and the more general acquired-divisor theorem, all linked to the original
recurrence. The strict Lean 4.33.1 replay and endpoint audits verify these statements with standard
axioms; the multiplier-location mechanism is shared with Cloitre’s conditional argument.

For prime 𝑝 ≥ 7, either 𝑝 mod 3 = 2 or 𝑝 mod 5 = 2 suffices. More generally, a divisor 𝑑 > 1 of
x(m) and 𝑝 − 2 with 1 ≤ 𝑚 ≤ 𝑝 − 3 suffices.

# OpenMath final submission: checked certificates and exact proof boundaries for Černý research

Prepared 2026-10-03 (Asia/Shanghai). This is a **partial contribution** to the
Černý problem, centered on existing Lean results. It does **not** solve the
general conjecture or give an improved upper bound for arbitrary synchronizing
automata. No new mathematical research was undertaken in submission preparation.

## Target and contribution

The target is the Černý conjecture: every synchronizing complete deterministic
automaton on n states has a reset word of length at most (n−1)². A reset word
maps all states to one state, with every original letter charged cost one.

The submission supplies kernel-checked potential and graph-certificate
soundness, an abstract three-anchor lower bound, exact finite C3/C4 subset
paths, a literal six-state Kari obstruction to inverse monotonicity and its
base length/phase facts, and a finite-depth reflection-hole certificate.
It includes an exhaustive declaration/axiom inventory and reproducible checks.
These results delimit proposed proof methods; the abstract hypotheses and
paper-to-automaton bridges are exposed explicitly.

The authoritative exact statements are reproduced verbatim from the actual
Lean declarations in [submission/THEOREMS.md](submission/THEOREMS.md), with
qualified names, source lines, source SHA-256 values and axiom dependencies.
[submission/theorems.json](submission/theorems.json) is the corresponding
machine-readable inventory. There are **100 theorem declarations in ten
authoritative compilation units**, including repeated helper declarations in
standalone files. This count is not a count of 100 new mathematical results.

    (walk : Walk (Edge (n-3)) ⟨n-3, true, true, true⟩ goal length)
    (terminal : cardinality goal = 1) : 3*n-4 ≤ length

theorem optimal_subset_path :
    goal (run move initial witness) ∧
    ∀ w : List Bool, goal (run move initial w) → witness.length ≤ w.length

theorem reset_needs_shrink (q : Fin 6) (word : List (Fin 2))
    (hFull : (run (singleton q) word).val = 63) :
    1 ≤ shrinkCount (singleton q) word

    (hFull : run (singleton q) word = 63) : 25 ≤ word.length

    SafeRun [] word

the original rows are a=[4,4,2,3,1,5], b=[1,5,3,4,2,0]. Lists are processed
in **inverse** order; the corresponding original word has reversed letters.
The kernel proves the literal one-step preimage correspondence. No generic
arbitrary-DFA composition/reset interface is claimed. Likewise the C3/C4
theorem is stated in its explicit subset-table system, with one-step fidelity.

`SafeRun` requires safety **before each processed letter**; it does not
require the final hole list to be safe. The unsafe result after the eight-letter
prefix is consistent with `no_avoid_first_eight`. Transferring it to avoidance
at a ninth concrete letter is a paper argument. The formal reflection file
does not state an arbitrary-M avoiding-word or reset theorem.
